Two of the sources said the intelligence is specific, including locations and targets, and has prompted contingency planning and several meetings in the past week. White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said the U.S. is “monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland.” The Office of the Director of National Intelligence declined to comment. Last week the Secret Service moved Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent into military housing over Iranian threats, joining several other administration officials.

headline: UN Secretary General Race: Where Things Stand The race to become the next UN Secretary General remains open after 8 informal Security Council straw polls. Costa Rica’s Rebeca Grynspan holds a lead in Security Council voting and is now the clear favorite on Polymarket, with a 45% chance of winning. Current Polymarket odds: Rebeca Grynspan (Costa Rica): 45% Lana Nusseibeh (UAE): 21% Rafael Grossi (Argentina): 16.5% María Fernanda Espinosa (Ecuador): 6.8% Despite entering the race 3 weeks late, Nusseibeh remains a leading contender. To secure the position, a candidate needs at least 9 Security Council votes and no veto from any of the 5 permanent members. The next straw poll is tentatively scheduled for November 19. A consensus candidate, negotiated compromise or failure to select a successor by December 31 all remain possible.
